title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree Summary Judgment And The Text There Is No God But Allah

questions.question: What central belief is declared at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: That only Allah is truly worthy of worship, and that He necessarily exists as the One and only God.

questions.question: How is the Prophet Muhammad described in relation to humanity?
questions.answer: He is presented as the most honored human being and a source of dignity for all people.

questions.question: What four features of the Prophet are given as signs supporting his testimony?
questions.answer: The greatness of the Qur’an given to him, the wide reach of his religion, his many excellences, and his lofty character.

questions.question: How does the passage show that even opponents support his truthfulness?
questions.answer: It says that even his enemies ended up confirming his outstanding qualities.

questions.question: What kind of evidence from the Prophet himself is mentioned?
questions.answer: His many clear miracles.

questions.question: Besides miracles, what else from his message is used as proof?
questions.answer: The many bright and decisive truths found in his religion.

questions.question: Which three groups are said to agree in confirming this testimony?
questions.answer: His family or spiritual heirs, his Companions, and the scholars of his community.

questions.question: What quality is emphasized about the scholars of the community?
questions.answer: They are described as people of proof and enlightened understanding.

questions.question: How does the passage connect Allah’s oneness with the Prophet’s witness?
questions.answer: It presents the Prophet’s life, message, and evidences as pointing to Allah’s unique unity.

questions.question: What is the overall purpose of the long statement in the passage?
questions.answer: To summarize a strong testimony that Allah exists, is one, and is affirmed through the Prophet’s mission and the agreement of the believers.

questions.question: In this passage, what does “Necessary Existent” mean about Allah?
questions.answer: It means Allah’s existence is not dependent on anything else and cannot be absent.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s uniqueness?
questions.answer: That He is single and without partner or equal.

questions.question: Why is the Prophet’s Qur’an mentioned as part of the proof?
questions.answer: Because its greatness and authority support the truth of the one who brought it.

questions.question: What does the wide spread of the Prophet’s religion suggest in the passage?
questions.answer: That his message has powerful truth and lasting influence.

questions.question: Why are the Prophet’s personal qualities included in the argument?
questions.answer: Because his moral excellence strengthens trust in his witness.

questions.question: What is meant by saying his miracles are both proving and proven?
questions.answer: They serve as evidence for his truth, and they are themselves accepted as real by trustworthy testimony.

questions.question: How do the truths of the religion function in this passage?
questions.answer: They act as strong intellectual and spiritual evidence supporting the message.

questions.question: What role does consensus play in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that many reliable groups agree on the same truth, which makes the testimony stronger.

questions.question: What is the main conclusion a reader should draw from the whole passage?
questions.answer: That the Prophet’s message gives a powerful, multi-layered proof of Allah’s existence and oneness.

questions.question: What statement of faith stands at the heart of the passage?
questions.answer: The affirmation that there is no deity but Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage present the Prophet’s rank without making him divine?
questions.answer: It gives him the highest human honor while keeping him in the role of witness and servant.

questions.question: What does the majesty of the Qur’an contribute to the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: It shows the greatness of the revelation connected to the Prophet and supports his reliability.

questions.question: How does the passage use the growth of Islam as evidence?
questions.answer: It treats the broad reach of the religion as a sign of the strength and truth of the message.

questions.question: What is the difference between miracles and truths of religion in the passage?
questions.answer: Miracles are extraordinary signs linked to the Prophet, while the truths of religion are enduring teachings that also confirm him.

questions.question: Why is the agreement of different groups important instead of only one group’s support?
questions.answer: Because support from several kinds of people makes the case broader and harder to dismiss.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the Companions from their inclusion in the consensus?
questions.answer: They are viewed as reliable witnesses who understood and affirmed the Prophet’s truth.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the scholars mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: They are seen as thoughtful investigators whose insight gives intellectual weight to the testimony.

questions.question: Does the passage rely only on emotional praise of the Prophet? Explain.
questions.answer: No. It includes honor and praise, but it also builds an argument through miracles, teachings, and agreement among reliable groups.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is the passage trying to strengthen in the reader?
questions.answer: Confidence in tawhid through the Prophet’s witness and the confirming testimony of the Muslim community.

questions.question: What is the main religious claim being affirmed in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah alone exists necessarily and is the only true God.

questions.question: Through whom is this claim especially indicated in the passage?
questions.answer: Through the Prophet Muhammad.

questions.question: What titles are used to show the Prophet’s high standing among people?
questions.answer: He is described as the pride of the world and the honor of the children of Adam.

questions.question: Name one outward sign and one inward sign used to support the Prophet’s truthfulness.
questions.answer: An outward sign is his miracles, and an inward sign is his noble character.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the testimony of enemies?
questions.answer: To show that his excellence was so clear that even opponents could not fully deny it.

questions.question: How do the “thousands of truths” differ from “hundreds of miracles” in the way they persuade?
questions.answer: The truths persuade through the content of the religion, while the miracles persuade through extraordinary signs.

questions.question: What is the effect of listing the family, Companions, and scholars together?
questions.answer: It presents support across generations and types of people, giving the testimony depth and breadth.

questions.question: How are the members of the Prophet’s community described at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: As people who possess evidence and enlightened insight.

questions.question: What does this passage suggest about the relationship between character and credibility?
questions.answer: High moral character strengthens the trustworthiness of a person’s religious witness.

questions.question: If a student summarized the passage as “a combined case for Allah’s oneness,” would that fit? Why?
questions.answer: Yes, because the passage gathers several kinds of proof into one unified testimony for Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What truth about Allah is repeated with more than one word in the passage?
questions.answer: His absolute oneness and uniqueness.

questions.question: Why might the passage use several honors for the Prophet instead of just one?
questions.answer: To show the fullness of his rank and the many ways he is distinguished.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the sovereignty of the Qur’an point to?
questions.answer: The powerful authority and greatness of the revelation brought by the Prophet.

questions.question: What does the expansiveness of the religion show in this argument?
questions.answer: That the message is not small or limited, but far-reaching and influential.

questions.question: How do the Prophet’s perfections and character work together as evidence?
questions.answer: They show both excellence in personal qualities and excellence in moral conduct.

questions.question: Why is enemy testimony especially persuasive?
questions.answer: Because praise from critics carries extra weight since they are less likely to exaggerate in his favor.

questions.question: What two broad categories of proof are named after the mention of enemy testimony?
questions.answer: Miracles and the truths contained in the religion.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the Prophet’s community of learning?
questions.answer: As a body of people marked by strong reasoning and spiritual clarity.

questions.question: What is the significance of agreement among multiple groups rather than isolated individuals?
questions.answer: It suggests a shared and well-established recognition of the same reality.

questions.question: What overall image of Islamic belief does this passage give?
questions.answer: A faith grounded in revelation, character, signs, and the united confirmation of trustworthy believers.

questions.question: What is the first thing the passage asks the reader to affirm about Allah?
questions.answer: That there is no god except Him.

questions.question: After affirming Allah’s existence, what further truth about Him is stressed?
questions.answer: That He is one and unique.

questions.question: Who is the main human witness named in support of this truth?
questions.answer: The Prophet Muhammad.

questions.question: What parts of the Prophet’s mission are used as evidence in this passage?
questions.answer: His Qur’an, his religion, his many virtues, his elevated character, and his miracles.

questions.question: What surprising source of support for the Prophet is mentioned?
questions.answer: The acknowledgment of his enemies.

questions.question: How does the passage combine personal evidence and communal evidence?
questions.answer: It mentions the Prophet’s own signs and qualities, then adds the agreement of major groups within the Muslim community.

questions.question: What communal groups are named as confirming the message?
questions.answer: The luminous ones among his family or followers, his Companions, and the verifying scholars of the ummah.

questions.question: What does the description of these groups suggest about the kind of confirmation they provide?
questions.answer: That their confirmation is informed, sincere, and based on insight and proof.

questions.question: Is the passage presenting a weak personal opinion or a strong shared testimony? Explain.
questions.answer: It presents a strong shared testimony because it rests on multiple forms of evidence and broad agreement.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the whole passage?
questions.answer: It is a compact declaration that Allah’s oneness is proven through the Prophet’s life, message, miracles, and the united witness of the faithful.
